evaluation_protocol: 5-fold StratifiedKFold on X_train (614 rows); final test set (154 rows) strictly quarantined
technical_selection_rationale: Logistic Regression was selected based strictly on Step 6 5-fold cross-validation evidence on the 614-row training partition. It achieved the highest mean Accuracy (0.7899 +/- 0.0194), highest Precision (0.7652 +/- 0.0605), highest F1-Score (0.6583 +/- 0.0231), and highest ROC-AUC (0.8434 +/- 0.0188) among all evaluated candidate models. Across the 5 folds, its recall standard deviation was 0.0152. While tree-based ensembles (Gradient Boosting and Random Forest) yielded higher recall (0.5981 and 0.5935 vs 0.5794, representing 4 and 3 fewer false negatives across 614 validation samples), they incurred more false positives (64 and 57 vs 39 for Logistic Regression) and lower mean ROC-AUC (0.8195 and 0.8209 vs 0.8434).

trade_off_analysis.recall_vs_precision: Gradient Boosting and Random Forest achieved 4 and 3 fewer false negatives respectively across the 614 training validation folds (86 and 87 vs 90 FNs for Logistic Regression). However, this marginal recall difference (+1.87% and +1.41%) was accompanied by an increase in false positives (64 and 57 FPs vs 39 for Logistic Regression). Logistic Regression maintained higher mean ROC-AUC (0.8434 vs 0.8195 and 0.8209) and the highest mean F1-score (0.6583).
trade_off_analysis.variance_stability: Logistic Regression exhibited lower recall standard deviation across folds (0.0152) than Gradient Boosting (0.0308) and XGBoost (0.0513) on this dataset.
trade_off_analysis.simplicity_and_calibration: Logistic Regression is a linear baseline model that outputs class probabilities directly via the logistic link function without additional ensemble parameters.
